# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 59 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_059_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 59

**1** Jesus said: "Look upon the Living One while you are alive,

**2** lest you die and seek to see him and be unable."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"The Living One"** — preserved as a title throughout (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA agree). The capitalization marks it as a divine designation.

**"Lest"** — LOGOS preferred over EMET's "so that you will not" for concision; PNEUMA's "otherwise" is acceptable but slightly paraphrastic.

**Theological Note:** The urgency of present vision vs. post-mortem inability is the theological core; all agents preserve it. The saying implies that spiritual vision is possible only during embodied life — death forecloses the opportunity.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Cf. Saying 1 (whoever finds the interpretation of these sayings will not taste death); John 8:51 ("if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death"). Thomas's version frames the imperative as a matter of timing rather than obedience.
